root_cause: Segment._split_cells guesses a starting index pos = int((cut / cell_length) * (len(text) - 1)) and then only scans forward. When double-width chars are front-loaded (e.g. '早乙女リリエル (CV: 徳井青）', 28 cells / 17 chars), the guess overshoots: at cut=7 it gives pos=4 with cell_len(text[:4])=8 > 7. The forward loop then hits the 'cell_pos > cut' branch at once and returns a left part of the wrong width ('早乙女リ ' = 9 cells instead of 7). Cuts 7, 9, 11, 13 and 14 are all wrong.
best_solution: Make the starting guess an under-estimate so the forward scan never starts past the cut: pos = int((cut / cell_length) * len(text)) - 1, clamped to 0 (and add a docstring). The walk then adds cells one char at a time and splits exactly at cut, or turns a straddled double-width char into two spaces. Reasoning from the statement: 'split cells' must return a left part with cell_len == cut for every cut. Write a loop over every cut on a mixed CJK+ASCII string, see the proportional guess overshoot, and either lower-bound the guess or start the scan at 0. Starting at 0 (a linear scan) is always correct. The gold's '-1' guess works for the tested strings but is still a heuristic.
acceptable_alternatives: Start the scan at pos=0/cell_pos=0 and keep the existing forward loop (v6, v7): fully correct and O(n), the lru_cache hides the cost. A full rewrite of the loop that splits at the first char where cell_pos+size > cut and puts spaces on both sides of a straddled wide char (v4) also passes.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_segment.py adds test_split_cells_mixed ('早乙女リリエル (CV: 徳井青）'), test_split_cells_doubles ('早'*20) and test_split_cells_single ('A'*20). Each checks, for every position in 1..cell_length-1, that Segment.split_cells(seg, position) returns a left part with cell_len == position and a right part with cell_len == cell_length - position. It imports rich.cells.cell_len. The existing test_split_cells_emoji cases must still pass, including the rule that a straddled double-width char becomes ' ' + ' '.
locating_signals: The statement names the method (Segment._split_cells), so the fix location is fully given: rich/segment.py. The linked Textual issue (a double-width character measured wrongly) points at CJK width. The statement gives no repro and does not say what is wrong.
our_outcome_summary: v4, v6 and v7 passed; v8 failed. v6/v7 replaced the proportional guess with pos=0, cell_pos=0 (about 3 lines, a correct linear scan). v4 rewrote the loop (1800 chars, it left a duplicated 'raise AssertionError' line) and still passed. v8 (117s, 26 calls) changed no behavior: its patch only adds a comment after the overflow branch, so test_split_cells_mixed fails with 'assert 9 == 7' (left='早乙女リ '). v8 most likely never reproduced the bug on mixed-width text and submitted a no-op.
generalizable_lesson: When a terse statement names a function as buggy but gives no repro, write a quick property check before editing: loop over every input position (every cut index, and mixed, all-wide and all-narrow data) and assert the invariant the name implies, e.g. len(left)==cut. Only submit once the check fails before the fix and passes after. Never submit a patch that only adds comments or docstrings. For estimate-then-scan code that only scans one way, make sure the estimate can never pass the target, or start the scan from 0.
